title: A knight on a new square
objective: Use a knight jump to capture a pawn in an unfamiliar position.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original transfer exercise
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Your knight starts on a different square this time. Look for a pawn it can capture with an L-shaped jump.
steps.coach_prompt: Take a moment to find your own move.

question.prompt: Capture a pawn with your knight.
hints: Find the knight and look two squares away, then one square across.
The knight on c4 can capture the pawn on b6.

tree.feedback: Yes. From c4 to b6 is two squares up and one across, and your knight captures the pawn.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal. Look again at the goal: Capture a pawn with your knight.

takeaway: A knight uses the same L-shaped jump wherever it starts.
